title: A Human-Centric Approach to Explainable AI for Personalized Education
extended_summary:
This doctoral thesis addresses a central barrier to the use of AI in education: although predictive models can support personalized learning and teaching, they are often not adopted in practice because their decisions are not sufficiently explainable or trustworthy to students, teachers, and other educational stakeholders. The work focuses on explainable AI (XAI) for personalized education, asking how educational AI systems can provide explanations that are accurate, consistent, actionable, and understandable to humans.

The thesis combines technical AI development with human-centered evaluation. It first studies student modeling at scale across 26 online courses with more than 100,000 students and millions of interactions, then evaluates five existing explainability methods and finds systematic disagreement among explainers on the same students and models. In response, it proposes several intrinsically interpretable or explanation-focused approaches: MultiModN, an interpretable multimodal modular model; InterpretCC, an interpretable mixture-of-experts model using adaptive sparsity; adversarial training to improve explainer consistency; and iLLuMinaTE, an LLM-XAI pipeline for generating user-friendly, actionable explanations.

The populations and contexts span online higher-education settings and expert stakeholder studies. Human studies reported in the thesis include semi-structured interviews with 26 university professors, evaluations by 56 teachers, interviews with 20 expert learning scientists, and actionability evaluations by 114 university students. The educational context is primarily online course environments, with stakeholders including both students and educators interacting with explanations derived from predictive models of student success and course behavior.

The main conclusion is that high predictive performance alone is insufficient for educational AI adoption; explainability must be aligned with human needs. The thesis finds that post-hoc explainers can be inconsistent and may not reliably support trust, while expert users value explanations for actionability but differ in what they consider trustworthy. Overall, the work argues for a human-centric shift toward inherently interpretable model designs, rigorous evaluation of explanation quality, and explanation systems that help users move from model outputs to meaningful educational action.

identified_tools.name: iLLuMinaTE
identified_tools.description: An LLM-XAI pipeline designed to translate model explanations into user-friendly, actionable, zero-shot explanations for personalized education.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a communication layer for explainable AI that provides mid-semester feedback explanations to university students based on educational prediction models and XAI outputs.

findings.finding_summary: The thesis reports that 114 university students evaluated the actionability of mid-semester feedback explanations generated with iLLuMinaTE. The abstract states that the system generated user-friendly, actionable explanations and that students evaluated their actionability, but no effect size, confidence interval, or quantitative comparative result is provided in the excerpt.
findings.measure: Student-evaluated actionability of mid-semester feedback explanations

identified_tools.name: MultiModN
identified_tools.description: An interpretable, modular, multimodal model for prediction and explanation that can handle missing data with fewer parameters.
identified_tools.use_case: Proposed and evaluated as an inherently interpretable student modeling approach for personalized learning and teaching, including educational prediction tasks.

identified_tools.name: InterpretCC
identified_tools.description: An interpretable mixture-of-experts model that uses adaptive sparsity to produce concise explanations while maintaining predictive performance.
identified_tools.use_case: Proposed and evaluated as an intrinsically interpretable model for educational prediction and explanation, including teacher perception studies of hybrid explanations.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic large language model functionality used to generate natural-language explanations from XAI outputs.
identified_tools.use_case: Used within the thesis as part of the iLLuMinaTE pipeline to generate user-friendly explanations; specific LLM families are mentioned in chapter figures/tables, but the thesis-level excerpt does not establish a single focal named product for the paper overall.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a doctoral thesis describing multiple empirical evaluations and human studies, but the provided excerpt does not give enough methodological detail or causal design information for strong causal claims about educational effectiveness. The reported evidence in the excerpt is largely mixed-methods and user-perception/actionability oriented.
impact_tier_rationale: The excerpt suggests promising and actionable outcomes, especially for iLLuMinaTE, but does not report effect sizes or clear quantitative learning gains. Impact is therefore unclear from the provided text.
